questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to go to UWA in Perth, Australia because they offer a lot of relevant environmental units. The units offers some perspectives on environmental issues that can't be found in the unit handbook at Copenhagen University. Additionally, the weather is nice in Australia and it is nice that they speak English (it makes both social and academic life a lot easier).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. They have a welcoming week at UWA when you arrive - where they are good at giving information. It is also possible to communicate with UWA's global learning office through email and facebook before arriving in AUS.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They helped me find accommodation through email before arriving. Also, they gave a good introduction to everything throughout the welcome week (first week in AUS).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: They had a housing crisis after covid-19, so it was actually quite difficult to find housing. However, there are multiple options. I stayed at an off-campus student accommodation called the Boulevard which was in the middle of the city with 20 minutes from campus. It was a five-bedroom shared apartment. If you're looking for a very social "kinda-american" experience, I've heard Trinity and Sct. Catherine's residential colleges at the campus are good. The Boulevard and Study Perth is nice to live at because you're close to nightlife and the city. However, if I could redo my accommodation situation; I would have tried to be patient (maybe live in a hostel the first couple of weeks) and then find a room in a shared-house through facebook or netoworking.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Housing is expensive. The good thing about living off-campus is that you're close to everything else.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a system that works fine. So just look through their unit handbook and register through the portal (that they'll help you access). In general, the global learning office guides you through everything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Whatever help is needed :)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You might need to have a backup plan with extra units if the timetables clash - but the GLO can help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The workload is bigger but I found the level a bit lower.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The workload is bigger because you're assessed throughout the semester (how depends on the units). I found the level a bit lower but I had to prepare for classes a lot more because I was assessed on participation in some of my units. Also, I had fewer classes a week than at UCPH - so more time was spent on making assignments and preparing for class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental History
Environmental Policy and Planning
Understanding Global Politics
Culture, Ecologies, Extinction: Environment and Society in a Time
of Crisis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Environmental History was very interesting and the teacher Joseph was very good. Also, the unit style was like a workshop with discussions - it was therefore a good opportunity to talk to other students. Description from the unit: "What factors have shaped human dealings with the natural world? How have people changed the environment? And how have different societies responded to environmental change over time? These are the questions at the heart of this unit, which offers an introduction to the flourishing field of environmental history."

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None unexpected really. I ended up purchasing a car with two other girls which has been amazing. It is quite expensive to rent one and very cheap to buy one (we just sold it for more than we bought it for).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive and alcohol is crazy expensive. Also, my housing was quite expensive (but that can be done cheaper).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some trips at the beginning for international students. They had a lot of sports that were possible to join (also, some for free for international students).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join as much as you can comprehend. Have a look at the active lifestyle program it offers multiple sports for free for international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Western Australia is amazing. Go to Exmouth or Margaret River if you get the chance.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Australian culture is not that different to Danish - so that wasn't difficult. Also, Australians are more outgoing and easy to talk to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Australians don't seem to go to uni to make friends, to be honest... So It is not like an "American-College-Experience". If you wanna socialize with local students I'd recommend you to live at a residential college.I got a job at a bakery and socialized with people from work - which was a really great experience for me. I'd definitely recommend that as well - you're allowed to work 40 hours every second week with a student visa.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very chill and outgoing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Bring more clothes than you think - the winter is longer than you think
- Go to the beach as much as possible and enjoy that the sun always sets over the ocean
- Double R at campus has really good coffee :)) (Australia in general has great (cheap) coffee and nice bakeries - so take advantage of that

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pica bar in CBD is great. Also, Miller and Baker (the place I worked) has rye bread!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being on your own in a country so far away is very rewarding. I think I've learned a lot from being independent. Also, the units I've taken were very rewarding because they gave me some interesting new perspectives on human-environment relationships. I think they've helped me come up with an idea for my bachelor's thesis.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going home again and leaving Perth.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
